acceptance: A bundle from any run carries the start and end samples; on a platform without load average the field is null, not absent, and a test covers that case.
Sampling happens outside every measured interval; the PR shows where, and a test or timing comparison shows power-test query timings are unchanged.
Smoke: two scale 0.01 runs through make heavy-run, one on a quiet host and one beside a deliberate CPU load, show clearly different recorded values.
The submission validator, the corpus inventory generator and the Explorer build accept bundles with and without the new fields, and the artifact privacy check passes.
The schema version changes as benchbox/core/results/schema_policy.py requires for an additive field, the result-format documentation lists the fields, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
context:
Origin: adversarial review on 2026-11-13 of work first left unfiled. The earlier reasons assumed a person at the keyboard; this item records the corrected disposition. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: a search of benchbox/core for getloadavg, load_avg, cpu_percent, cpu_steal and thermal finds nothing.

Decision gate (before coding): confirm from schema_policy.py whether an additive environment field needs a schema version step, and that the Explorer read model tolerates it; if it would break published-bundle parity, stop and report. Result-schema code may be a soundness path that needs the external reviewer; say so in the PR.

Durations and sample timestamps use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time() and elapsed_seconds(); wall clocks are for audit only.

Verification rubric: pass only if the two-run smoke shows a visible difference and the timing-unchanged evidence is in the PR.

If publish-result-bundle-json-schema-20261112 proceeds, its schema must include these fields.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: a result bundle records the machine (CPU, memory, operating system) but nothing about how busy it was. A person usually knows what else is running; an agent, or several agents sharing one host, does not. This repository's own heavy-work lock exists because overlapping jobs exhausted a 16 GiB machine, yet a user's bundle from such a host looks the same as one from an idle host.

Outcome: the environment block records load average, available memory and swap in use at run start and run end, taken with psutil (already a core dependency), with an explicit null where the platform cannot report a value. The integrity validator reports the values as INFO.

Non-goals: no threshold, no warning level, no refusal to run and no active calibration workload. Thresholds wait until published bundles carry enough of this data to choose them.
